result.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) generally rely on sampling temperature to regulate the amount of randomness in their outputs. Mainstream methods for selecting temperature typically involve fixed, heuristic global settings and context or token-level calibration, rather than a geometrically interpretable representation of the communicative scenario. In this work, we introduce a simple and interpretable temperature selection framework, the \textbf{Scenario-Actor}, which adapts decoding to the inferred situational characteristics. Scenario-Actor extracts scenario-relevant structures from Transformer hidden states and determines the temperature from scenario embedding, a structured geometric representation of the communicative setting. Empirical results show that on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Scenario-Actor achieves strong goal-completion performance in interactive social scenarios, significant gains on open-ended instruction following, and competitive performance on multi-turn conversation compared to multiple baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Scenario-Actor 温度选择框架：从 Transformer 隐状态中抽取情境相关结构，构造几何化的 scenario embedding，据此自适应地确定解码温度，并在 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 的交互社交、开放式指令跟随与多轮对话任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「从隐状态读出结构化表示并据此调节生成」的做法，可能与 LVR 中依据内部 latent 状态动态控制解码或推理步长的思路相通，可供核查；但该工作为纯文本、不涉及视觉证据筛选，联系较弱。
